approach.method_basis: The Parent builds molecules by differentiating through a soft version of their structure. It represents each scored molecule as a graph of whole rings and individual atoms, preserves the interior, and makes the identities and presence of selected terminal units and expansion sites adjustable probabilities. A graph encoder learned from unlabeled molecules stays frozen, while a ridge readout is refitted on the current objective's accepted scores. Starting molecules are sampled with a preference for high score rank. The Parent takes bounded gradient steps that increase this readout's predicted value, retains the best relaxed state, then samples structural decisions and compatible attachments to assemble valid, distinct molecules. Accepted products enter the archive and can become later starting structures. The observed limitation is that increasing this point prediction often fails to produce a better assembled molecule.
approach.novelty: The added mechanism is ascent of a lower confidence bound on structural gain. A Gaussian posterior over the existing ridge coefficients estimates how uncertain a proposed change in the frozen graph features is. Structural ascent subtracts one posterior standard deviation of that gain, so a promising but poorly supported direction receives a smaller gradient contribution. The fitted mean remains the Parent's ridge prediction, and the resulting probabilities still drive its existing sampling and assembly process. This lineage contains only its root so far; no sibling has tested coefficient uncertainty inside structural ascent. The experiment asks whether that uncertainty changes the structural updates before sampling, and whether the resulting proposals transfer more reliably to actual improvements.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent n-0e1f7686dea8 has an optimistic structural objective: every one of its 175 optimizations increased the retained relaxed prediction, but mean accepted child-minus-source score was negative on every objective. Only 267 of 824 predicted discrete improvements actually beat their generating sources, and only 380 of all 1450 emitted proposals did so. The immutable observation also reports that chronological prediction error exceeded final in-sample fit error on every task; for zaleplon_mpo the respective RMSE values were 0.135969779 and 0.0515970171356. Its completed supplied replica has macro score 0.361872161920233. These are observations from one screening replica, not an estimate of reliability across seeds. They establish weak transfer from a confident point prediction to evaluated improvements, while leaving its causes unresolved: coefficient uncertainty, representation error, relaxed-to-discrete sampling and attachment choices may all contribute. The current change addresses only unsupported readout directions. The brief has no Mechanism Clusters and the lineage has no earlier Child that settles this hypothesis.
hypothesis: Replace point-estimate structural ascent with ascent of a numerically smoothed lower confidence bound on relaxed structural gain, subtracting one standard deviation computed from the full Gaussian coefficient posterior associated with the Parent's accepted-only ridge readout and differentiating that uncertainty through the frozen graph encoder.

finding_summary.headline: Uncertainty changed every relaxation, but the mean score fell from 0.3619 to 0.3079
finding_summary.insights:
This experiment establishes that coefficient uncertainty can change structural search before sampling and survive every downstream assembly step. It also shows that correcting this particular source of uncertainty is insufficient to remove prediction optimism or preserve the best final score. The strongest illustration is DRD2: 188 of 290 proposals beat their source, yet the search settled around a much lower score. The molecular assessment describes increasingly crowded polyacetals with late scores near 0.028858, while the Parent's stronger products belonged to a different biaryl/amine series. Repeated small improvements inside a weak chemical family can therefore make source-beating rates look favorable while valuable regions remain unreached.

The evidence leaves open whether the uncertainty penalty restricted productive exploration, whether early stochastic differences redirected the search, or whether structural information missing from the frozen features dominated the remaining errors. The posterior covers coefficient uncertainty conditional on an empirical noise estimate; it does not cover attachment choices, stereochemistry or the gap between a relaxed state and its assembled molecule. The generated structures still exhibit the reactive attachments and unspecified configurations identified by the molecular assessment. Preserving access to alternative core families and representing attachment environments remain worth testing. One paired seed cannot establish the repeatability of the four gains or the DRD2 loss.
finding_summary.results:
The intended mechanism ran throughout this screening replica. All 150 accepted-score posterior fits were valid, all 145 feedback updates changed the full coefficient covariance, and all 152 structural optimizations changed their retained categorical distributions relative to the same starting state's mean-only ascent. Every one of the 1,450 emitted proposals used those changed distributions. All eligible nonzero uncertainty corrections reduced the raw gradient's uncertainty directional derivative, and every optimization retained a positive confidence gain; none needed a fallback.

On the single supplied seed, macro Top-1 fell from 0.361872 to 0.307903, a loss of 0.053969. Four objectives improved: zaleplon_mpo from 0.380139 to 0.394051, deco_hop from 0.589062 to 0.602445, median_2 from 0.180051 to 0.183284, and sitagliptin_mpo from 0.234090 to 0.330875. The loss came from drd2_docking, which fell from 0.426020 to 0.028858. Both runs completed all five 300-evaluation tasks with valid, distinct batches.

Local improvement became more frequent: 447 of 1,450 proposals beat their generating molecule, compared with 380 for the Parent. Predicted improvements were realized 41.1% of the time, up from 32.4%. Their average actual score change nevertheless worsened from -0.025853 to -0.031192, and average overstatement of assembled source-relative gains rose from 0.023479 to 0.034251. Better local hit rates did not produce a better overall search result.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich scaffold series with reactive attachments; the largest products are crowded polyacetals with undefined stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: For n-b3517f183781, the supplied seed-0 trajectories each contain 300 distinct recorded molecules, including 290 optimizer proposals. Every proposal set has ring_closure_rate 1.0 and branch_rate 1.0. The main products are dihydropyrazole-thioureas, extended heteroaryl-substituted indoles, quinoline ethers linked to substituted piperidines, silylmethyl-substituted indole carboxamides, and heavily elaborated polyacetals. Rings, heteroatoms, aromatic groups and saturated amine rings are readily represented. Aromatic-atom presence rates are 1.0 for zaleplon_mpo, deco_hop and median_2, 0.9828 for sitagliptin_mpo, and 0.3379 for the predominantly saturated drd2_docking series. These are presence readings from SMILES text, not aromatic atom fractions or perceived ring counts. The output has many distinct decorations but narrow core families within each trajectory. Ordinary medicinal scaffolds coexist with O-F and N-F bonds, peroxides, chloromethyl ethers, sulfenyl chlorides, primary hydrosilanes and, in a late polyacetal, an explicit carbanion. The most congested polyacetals are difficult to regard as routine synthetic targets. All proposal sets have stereocentre_rate 0.0: configurations are unspecified even where the connectivity implies stereogenic carbons. This does not mean the molecules are achiral. The qualitative quality labels describe the recorded structures; no synthesis, conformer, docking-pose or new property calculation was performed. All supplied objectives are covered. The score readings below are associations in these trajectories and the Parent comparison, not proof of individual substituent effects or a missing target-specific pharmacophore.

per_task.generated_character: Mostly compact to moderately sized aryl-substituted dihydropyrazoles carrying a thiourea linkage. The leading series has two aryl arms, phenols, methyl substitution and small fluorinated groups; the best molecule at evaluation 277 has an N-methylated aryl-thiourea, an aryl fluoride and a fluoromethyl ether. The fluoromethyl ether has a carbon between oxygen and fluorine. Other high and late examples instead contain hydroperoxides, O-O-S or O-S attachments and aryl thiols. Mean SMILES length is 44.5, with maximum 67; aromatic and ring presence rates are both 1.0 and halogen presence is 0.6517. The core is recognizably makeable organic chemistry, while several terminal attachments have questionable stability. Relative to Parent n-0e1f7686dea8, the leading chemistry remains a dihydropyrazole family but retains the thiourea and phenolic aryl groups, where the Parent leaders used an aminomethyl-pyridyl cap and a furyloxyphenyl arm.
liabilities: Evaluation 59 contains an aryl hydroperoxide, and the final molecule contains an O-O-S chain. These introduce reactive oxygen-oxygen bonds into otherwise familiar scaffolds.
Evaluation 289 carries an aryl sulfenyl chloride. Such an S-Cl attachment is a materially different stability concern from the ordinary carbon-bound fluorine in the best molecule.

Some lower-scoring products crowd extra saturated or heteroaromatic rings around the same core. The individual fragments are familiar, but the complete attachment patterns are less convincing synthetic targets.
missing_features: Comparably successful alternative core connectivities that retain the compact polar/aromatic arrangement are not demonstrated among the leading molecules; the highest-scoring set stays with the dihydropyrazole-thiourea family.
Defined configurations at the substituted dihydropyrazole carbons are absent. The supplied records contain no comparison from which a stereochemical score preference could be inferred.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The supplied phenolic triaryl dihydropyrazole-thiourea starts at 0.1501184006136499. The less aryl-heavy, phenol-bearing evaluation 56 reaches 0.3649319479033378, and evaluation 277 reaches 0.39405142067435733. Bulky variants carrying additional saturated amine rings or multiple heterocycles are much lower: evaluation 11 is 6.600561276614438e-07, and evaluation 36, which also lacks the thiocarbonyl, is 1.6543725850431745e-11. The visible preference is for a compact polar/aromatic arrangement within this family; it does not establish that adding halogens, thiols or peroxide bonds is generally beneficial. The final O-O-S-bearing product scores 0.3286687595331667. The Parent maximum was 0.380138751942517 with different decorations on a related core, showing another locally favorable chemical arrangement without identifying a unique required substituent.

per_task.generated_character: The leading products are extended, densely substituted indoles linked through a fluorinated benzylic amine to a phenyl-triazole-oxadiazole chain. They carry formate esters, methoxy or chloromethyl ethers and O-F groups; the best entry also replaces the indole N-H with N-F. These are large aromatic assemblies, with mean SMILES length 67.6, maximum 98, and aromatic/ring presence rates of 1.0. Halogen presence is 0.8172. The trajectory also contains the fused pyrimidinedione family seen in the Parent, so more than one supplied core is represented. The Child leaders are the indole series, whereas the Parent maximum came from a heteroaryl-decorated fused dione/benzoate series. Plain indole amides are plausible synthetic scaffolds; the combination of unusual reactive substituents makes the leading decorated products questionable.
liabilities: O-F bonds recur throughout the leading set, and the maximum also has an N-F bond. These are reactive heteroatom-halogen attachments, distinct from ordinary aryl or alkyl fluorides.
The best molecule combines a chloromethyl ether with a formate ester. These introduce an electrophilic attachment and an additional hydrolysis site.
Dense substitution of the fused ring and the long heteroaryl arm would require substantial synthetic control; a valid-looking connectivity does not establish an accessible route.
missing_features: The leading digest entries do not demonstrate a comparably successful version of the extended heteroaryl arrangement with conventional stable O/N substituents replacing its O-F and occasional N-F attachments.
Less extended, partly saturated alternative geometries with comparable scores are not demonstrated among the leaders; most of their variation adds or decorates heteroaromatic rings.
The stereogenic fluorinated benzylic amine linkage is left without a defined configuration. Its stereochemical contribution is untested in these records.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The supplied trimethoxy indole carboxanilide scores 0.5464020559680183, and the hydroxymethoxy-decorated carboxanilide at evaluation 13 scores 0.5370762711864407. Higher entries replace the carboxamide environment and add the extended nitrogen-rich heteroaryl arm: evaluation 60 is 0.5868885220262403 and evaluation 143 is 0.5887188327797166. Evaluation 215 reaches 0.6024454725710509 with N-F, O-F and chloromethyl-ether chemistry. The Parent maximum is 0.5890616392238477 on a different core family. The final extended indole remains at 0.5752439550103852. The observed gradient favors this extended aromatic/polar arrangement over the simpler carboxanilides, but simultaneous substitutions prevent assignment of the gain to any single reactive bond.

per_task.generated_character: The Child trajectory elaborates a protected-sugar-like polycyclic acetal framework into exceptionally crowded polyacetals. The leading structures retain the oxygen-rich core and attach many saturated or partly unsaturated nitrogen rings, cyclic ethers, sulfur heterocycles, some aromatic azoles and a primary SiH3 hydrosilane. Several carbons carry bulky ring substituents on an already complex fused/spiro acetal framework. Mean SMILES length is 100.7 and maximum 175. Ring presence is 1.0, aromatic-text presence 0.3379, charge presence 0.5483 and halogen presence 0.0517. The relatively low aromatic-text rate is consistent with the dominant saturated/partly unsaturated chemistry; it is not evidence of few rings. Basic amine centers are abundant in the later structures. The heavy congestion and unspecified stereochemistry make the leading products synthetically implausible as routine proposals. The Parent leaders instead use halogenated biaryl, pyrrolidine and morpholine/thiomorpholine chemistry with sulfenamide and aminal linkages.
liabilities: Multiple bulky substituents around acetal and ring-junction carbons create severe congestion and a difficult synthetic and stereochemical problem.
The primary SiH3 group is carried into the leading structures. It introduces reactive Si-H functionality without any supplied evidence about isolation or stability of these compounds.

Late products include unusual explicitly charged nitrogen environments, and evaluation 298 also has a localized carbon anion. That carbon anion is a different concern from ordinary protonation of the many amines; charge presence alone is not a defect.
missing_features: The Child leaders do not show the more compact aryl/basic-amine arrangement associated with the higher-scoring Parent series. Saturated amine rings themselves are already well represented.

A simplified scaffold presenting a limited set of polar and ionizable groups is missing from the leading polyacetal series; the nearly unchanged late scores do not establish which of its many appended groups are useful.

Defined relative and absolute stereochemistry of the polyacetal framework is absent, despite extensive saturated stereogenic connectivity. The strings do not specify a single three-dimensional product.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The supplied polyacetal scores 0.01605857048900594. Early lightly edited polyacetals are lower, including evaluation 11 at 0.01170760926407444 and evaluation 20 at 0.00968305889859544. The recorded progression accompanies extensive ring and nitrogen-containing appendage growth. The highest excerpted products occupy the very narrow range 0.028858249829473083 to 0.02885836184393584 despite substantial differences in pendant rings. The final molecule is 0.028856581210309352. These records support a local association with elaboration and heterocycle addition, while the late values provide little chemical discrimination among the resulting giant structures. The Parent maximum was 0.42602011617052177 on its biaryl/amine series. The Child therefore lacks that higher-scoring chemical family among its leaders. No pose or contact information is supplied, so the Child scores cannot identify productive binding interactions or show that further ring growth supplies them.

per_task.generated_character: A narrow family of quinoline-methyl ethers joined to substituted anilines and N-methylpiperidines. Most leading examples preserve an aryl carboxamide connection to the piperidine; a nearly leading alternative uses a reduced tertiary-aniline/alkylamine connection. The terminal groups include aldehydes, a methyl ketone, carboxylic acid, amides and hydrazides. Phenols, hydroxymethyl groups and occasional imidazole decoration add polarity. Mean SMILES length is 61.1, maximum 85, with aromatic/ring presence rates of 1.0. These are moderately large, recognizably medicinal scaffolds with an accessible basic ring center. The acid at evaluation 98 demonstrates access to an ordinary strongly polar terminus. The Parent leaders retain the same overall quinoline-ether/anilide/piperidine family, usually with an added imidazolidine on the central aryl ring.
liabilities: The best molecule contains an aryl hydroperoxide, which is a reactive O-O substituent rather than an ordinary phenol.

Aliphatic aldehydes recur in high and final entries and add oxidation and nucleophile-reactivity liabilities. The high-scoring carboxylic acid shows that such an aldehyde is not the only sampled favorable terminus.
Other leading variants introduce an O-S attachment or a hydrazide. Their presence expands polar chemistry but does not by itself establish stability or an accessible synthesis.
missing_features: A comparably successful alternative core family is not demonstrated among the leaders; both Child and Parent remain near the quinoline-ether/aniline/piperidine architecture.
Defined configurations at the substituted piperidine carbons are absent. The records cannot say whether their relative or absolute stereochemistry affects the objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The supplied quinoline/piperidine hydroxamate scores 0.1569767171139282. A more heavily substituted hydroxamate at evaluation 38 scores 0.1265764400205477. Higher entries keep the N-methylpiperidine and oxygenated aromatic regions while changing terminal groups: the carboxylic acid at evaluation 98 reaches 0.1808552681169606, the reduced-linker aldehyde at evaluation 255 reaches 0.1829453977110258, and the aldehyde/hydroperoxide/imidazole entry at evaluation 139 reaches 0.18328441832511358. These chemically different termini give similar reported scores, so neither an aldehyde nor a peroxide is established as necessary. The Parent maximum is 0.18005061593636776 in the same broad family. The final aminomethyl-substituted piperidine product scores 0.15129298547684675, illustrating that further polar and amine decoration does not consistently preserve the favorable local arrangement.

per_task.generated_character: The highest-scoring products are compact to moderately sized indole carboxanilides with a fluorinated phenyl ring, phenolic or aniline substitution on the indole benzene ring, and a silylmethyl ether. The latter is an oxygen-methylene-SiH3 linkage, not a conventional oxygen-bound trialkylsilyl protecting group. This motif recurs throughout the best digest entries. The core is largely aromatic with few saturated atoms; mean proposal SMILES length is 56.1, maximum 84, aromatic presence 0.9828, ring presence 1.0 and halogen presence 0.7207. The full trajectory also samples large acetal and fused-dione derivatives with very low scores. The ordinary indole amide framework is synthetically credible, but the primary hydrosilane and some peripheral heteroatom attachments make the complete products questionable. The Parent also favored indole derivatives; its maximum combined an N-SiH3 attachment with an O-linked aziridine, whereas the Child leaders favor the silylmethyl ether.
liabilities: Primary SiH3 hydrosilanes recur across the best molecules. Their Si-H reactivity and behavior in these complete structures are unresolved by the supplied SMILES and scores.

Some high or late entries add N-S, N-F or O-F attachments, and evaluation 295 carries an explicit phenolate. These changes introduce reactive bonds or a specified ionization state that a score alone does not chemically justify.

Strongly unfavorable late products retain the core and silicon motif while adding bulky substituents. The favorable arrangement is sensitive to its surrounding chemistry; presence of the recurring motif is insufficient.
missing_features: The leading excerpt does not demonstrate a similarly successful conventional replacement for the primary hydrosilane ether. The data show association with that motif, without establishing that it is chemically required.

A comparably successful alternative core geometry retaining the modest size and polar/aromatic arrangement is absent from the leading set. Large ring additions frequently move the sampled chemistry away from that favorable region.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The supplied trimethoxy indole carboxanilide scores 0.00012094961439027578. The silylmethyl/phenol variant at evaluation 44 scores 0.24323049964971696, the less methoxy-decorated phenol at evaluation 110 reaches 0.3188638798296843, and its difluoroanilide counterpart at evaluation 241 reaches 0.32964789455035565. The amino-substituted indole at evaluation 131 reaches 0.3308753645714267. The visible favorable region combines modest size, the indole/anilide arrangement, small polar substitution and the silylmethyl group; it does not prove a causal benefit from silicon itself. The charged acetal at evaluation 54 scores 6.520749754415915e-65, while late indoles with extra bulky ring decoration at evaluations 296 and 297 fall to 1.3225096655844806e-12 and 1.3601291579115854e-12. The trajectory median is 4.2e-05 and the final molecule scores 0.009046134500032013, so the favorable chemical region is narrow. The Parent maximum was 0.23408968632790841 in a differently decorated, still unusual indole series.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The leading extended indole contains O-F, N-F and chloromethyl-ether chemistry. Dihydropyrazole and quinoline series contain peroxides, and a leading dihydropyrazole contains a sulfenyl chloride. Primary SiH3 groups recur in both a compact indole series and the giant polyacetals. These are concrete attachment liabilities within recognizable scaffolds; ring availability is already rich.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently maintain stable bond environments when it combines otherwise familiar fragments.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent the full local attachment environment and provide conventional stable replacements that preserve the sampled polar and hydrophobic arrangement. Let accepted feedback test those alternatives, while distinguishing ordinary carbon-bound halogens, stable sulfur chemistry and common ionized amines from reactive heteroatom-halogen, peroxide or localized carbanion environments.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The polyacetal population has mean SMILES length 100.7 and maximum 175, with many pendant heterocycles, charged nitrogen environments and an SiH3 group. Its late reported scores lie close to 0.028858 despite substantial appendage changes. Elsewhere, compact indole and dihydropyrazole variants coexist with much lower-scoring derivatives carrying extra rings.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not demonstrate effective simplification of a crowded scaffold while retaining its useful polar and amine features.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide molecule-level contraction and rearrangement options as well as expansion, so a smaller scaffold can present a similar set of polar and ionizable groups. Track accumulated size and attachment congestion when proposing additional rings; task-local evidence must determine whether greater complexity is useful.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Each supplied trajectory records 300 distinct molecules, yet its leaders repeatedly retain an indole, dihydropyrazole, quinoline-ether/piperidine or polyacetal core from the supplied starting chemistry. Different input core families can appear, but much of the apparent diversity is peripheral substitution, heteroaryl extension and terminal-group exchange.
transferable_gaps.gap: Distinct proposed strings do not translate into broad access to alternative core geometry within a trajectory.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make alternative central ring connectivities and linker geometries accessible while preserving favorable functional relationships observed in accepted molecules. Assess chemical diversity at the core and attachment-topology level alongside canonical identity, allowing score feedback to choose among geometrically distinct series.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every proposal set has stereocentre_rate 0.0. The cited substituted dihydropyrazoles, fluorinated benzylic amines, substituted piperidines and crowded polyacetals nevertheless contain stereogenic connectivity. The absence is stereochemical specification, not saturated carbon or three-dimensional potential.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not express defined stereochemical products even when its connectivity creates stereogenic centers.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support explicit configuration and its preservation through structural changes so that emitted identities can denote individual stereoisomers. Evaluate any stereochemical preference through the same accepted-feedback process; these trajectories provide no evidence for choosing a particular configuration.

method_name: DST: gradient-guided construction through relaxed scaffolding trees
method_thesis: Anchor the method in Differentiable Scaffolding Tree: relax molecular substructure identity and existence into continuous variables, ascend a structural surrogate, and sample discrete structures from the optimized variables. [Fu et al., Sections 3.1-3.3](https://wenhao-gao.github.io/assets/publications/2021_DST_ICLR/paper.pdf) describe this proposal mechanism. For our adaptation, derive an atom/ring token alphabet and train a compact graph encoder by masked-substructure reconstruction solely on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Freeze that encoder and fit a regularized linear scalar readout using only the current objective's accepted observations, updating the readout after feedback. Select scored molecules as local starting structures; hold their internal scaffold context fixed while optimizing relaxed leaf replacement, deletion and expansion variables through the surrogate. Keep surrogate parameters fixed during each structural optimization. Sample edited trees and compatible attachment choices stochastically, assemble new molecules, and repeat generation until the announced batch contains distinct valid structures. The token alphabet supports construction; complete corpus molecules are never retrieved or ranked, and attachment combinations are sampled rather than exhaustively enumerated. Accepted feedback updates both the scored archive and the readout. The hypothesis is that useful structural gradients concentrate new proposals toward real improvements quickly enough to increase the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. Reliable gradients from scarce labels and faithful transfer from relaxed to assembled structures are unproven prerequisites.

method_references.title: Tianfan Fu, Wenhao Gao, Cao Xiao, Jacob Yasonik, Connor W. Coley, and Jimeng Sun. Differentiable Scaffolding Tree for Molecular Optimization. ICLR 2022. Sections 3.1-3.3 describe the anchor; Section 4 reports the larger labeled-training prerequisite that this adaptation must replace.
